lines.text: The robot's code runs in a loop, fifty times a second: once every twenty milliseconds.
Each time, Drive To Pose asks four questions.
One: where is the goal? It asks every loop, because the goal may have moved.
Two: how far is it? A straight arrow from robot to goal.
Three: how fast should I go? The heart of this video.
Four: how much may my velocity change this loop? That's physics, from video one.
The answers become one arrow: the velocity the robot is told to drive.
Twenty milliseconds later, it throws them away and asks again.
No plan is stored. Its only memory is the last velocity it asked for.
Far away the arrow is long. Close in, it shrinks. On the mark, it's gone.
